svg.aria-label: Polynomial identity theorem and difference polynomial proof
svg.title: Polynomial identity theorem and difference polynomial proof
svg.desc: Four staged panels: two quadratics agreeing at three distinct points, the difference polynomial d(x) having three zeros, contradiction with the degree bound on non-zero polynomials, and deduction of the zero polynomial.

g.text: Two polynomials deg(p) ≤ 2 and deg(q) ≤ 2 agree at x₁, x₂, x₃: p(xᵢ) = q(xᵢ)
2 · Define difference polynomial d(x) = p(x) - q(x)
• d(x) has degree at most two: deg(d) ≤ 2 (or d is zero polynomial).
• d(x) evaluates to zero at three inputs: d(x₁) = 0, d(x₂) = 0, d(x₃) = 0.
Theorem: A NON-ZERO polynomial of degree ≤ 2 has AT MOST TWO distinct zeros.
If d(x) were non-zero, having 3 distinct zeros would contradict the theorem!
4 · Conclusion: d(x) ≡ 0 identically, so p(x) = q(x) everywhere
Distinction: zero polynomial 0(x) has all zero coefficients and infinite zeros;
the "at most two zeros" bound applies strictly to non-zero polynomials.
